less:0.en: The Manager always said *less* is more when stacking the shelves — fewer items up front, room to breathe. I tried it at two in the morning, arranging the rice crackers in a neat little row. A sleepy old man shuffled in, stared at my work for a long moment, and smiled like I had done something right.
less:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我货架上的东西____一点反而更好看，一位老爷爷半夜进来后对此露出了赞许的微笑。
less:0.hook: The old man comes every single night — but never buys a thing.
less:0.line: 'Trust me, *less* really does look better on a shelf like this.'

information:0.en: A woman rushed in at midnight and asked for *information* about the bus route outside. I checked the small notice board by the door, then my phone, then called Tang over. Tang pointed at a hand-drawn map taped to the counter that I had completely missed. The woman laughed softly and thanked us both.
information:0.cnHint: 一位女士半夜跑来询问公交路线的____，我找了半天，同事阿糖一眼就发现了柜台上贴着的手绘地图。
information:0.hook: She folded that map and slipped it into her pocket before walking away.
information:0.line: 'Do you have any *information* about the last bus tonight?'

paragraph:0.en: A student sat on the step outside for an hour, notebook open, chewing his pen. He finally came in and bought a coffee, then asked me to read one *paragraph* of his essay aloud to see how it sounded. I read it slowly. He listened, eyes closed, nodding like it was music. Then he crossed out the whole thing.
paragraph:0.cnHint: 一位学生请我朗读他作文里的一个____，听完后他却把整段都划掉了。
paragraph:0.hook: He came back the next night with a brand-new first sentence.
paragraph:0.line: 'Could you read this *paragraph* out loud for me, just once?'

look:0.en: Tang gave me a certain *look* when I put the hot drinks on the wrong shelf — eyebrows up, lips pressed together, very patient. I moved them without a word. Later a regular came in, grabbed a warm can from the right spot, and said the store felt more settled lately. Tang gave me the same look, but softer.
look:0.cnHint: 同事阿糖用一个特别的____示意我把热饮放错了位置，后来一位常客夸店里感觉更整洁了。
look:0.hook: Tang has a whole silent language I am only beginning to learn.
look:0.line: 'Give me that *look* again and I will move it faster next time.'

benefit:0.en: The Manager explained that keeping the store warm all night was not just for comfort — it was a *benefit* for the elderly neighbours who had nowhere else to sit. An old woman arrived at three in the morning with a paper bag of leftover bread and quietly placed it on the counter for us.
benefit:0.cnHint: 店长说通宵开着暖气是对附近老人们的一种____，一位老奶奶深夜送来了面包作为回报。
benefit:0.hook: She left before I could learn her name.
benefit:0.line: 'The warmth here is a real *benefit* for people on cold nights.'

contain:0.en: A small boy knocked over a stand of sweets near the door. I rushed over to help, trying to *contain* the rolling candies before they reached every corner of the store. We caught most of them. He looked ready to cry until I held up the one candy that had escaped under the door and made it wave hello.
contain:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩把糖果架碰倒了，我赶紧试着____四处滚动的糖果，还用一颗逃跑的糖果逗他笑了。
contain:0.hook: His mother appeared in the doorway holding a slightly guilty smile.
contain:0.line: 'Help me *contain* these before they roll under the fridge!'

direction:0.en: A cyclist stopped outside and knocked on the glass, looking lost. I stepped out and gave her *direction* to the riverside path, using a pen to draw arrows on her paper bag. She repeated each turn back to me like a song. Then she rode off, turned left instead of right, and cheerfully vanished into the dark.
direction:0.cnHint: 一位骑车的女士迷路了，我给她指了去河边小路的____，但她骑走后马上走错了方向。
direction:0.hook: She waved back at me without slowing down at all.
direction:0.line: 'Thank you for the *direction* — I think I had it backwards the whole time.'

attach:0.en: Tang showed me how to *attach* the new price tags — a small loop of tape folded back on itself so the tag sits flat and peels off clean. It sounds simple. I used too much tape on my first try and pulled a little paint off the shelf. Tang did not laugh out loud, but their shoulders were shaking.
attach:0.cnHint: 阿糖教我怎样____价格标签，我第一次用了太多胶带，把货架上的漆都粘掉了一点。
attach:0.hook: The bare patch on the shelf is still there, and I see it every shift.
attach:0.line: 'You only need this much tape to *attach* a tag — truly, that is enough.'

derive:0.en: Around 2 a.m., an old man spreads a worn notebook on the counter and works through columns of numbers. He tells me he can *derive* real joy from simple math — that solving a row of figures feels better than sleep. Tang leans over, impressed. The old man smiles and flips to a page filled with tiny drawings of cats.
derive:0.cnHint: 一位老人深夜在柜台上算数，说他能从数学中____出真正的快乐。
derive:0.hook: But why does every cat drawing have a small key around its neck?
derive:0.line: 'You can *derive* real happiness from numbers, young one — try it.'

report:0.en: A teenage girl rushes in just before three and drops a folded paper on the counter. 'Can you hold this?' She looks pale. It is her school *report*, and one grade is circled in red ink. I tuck it safely under the register. Tang gives her a warm cup of soup without being asked.
report:0.cnHint: 一个女生把她的____放在柜台上，请我帮她保管，脸色有些苍白。
report:0.hook: She never came back for it before sunrise.
report:0.line: 'My *report* is bad — please don't let my mum see it tonight.'

research:0.en: A young woman in a big coat sets up a small voice recorder next to the snack shelf. She says she is doing *research* on what people buy at 3 a.m. and why. I watch her note down every item I scan. She buys only a single boiled egg and looks very satisfied.
research:0.cnHint: 一位年轻女士在零食架旁做____，记录深夜顾客买什么东西。
research:0.hook: Her recorder was still running when she forgot it on the shelf.
research:0.line: 'My *research* shows that night people always choose salty over sweet.'

different:0.en: Lin from the store across the street wanders in at midnight, hands in pockets. He stares at our shelf of hot drinks for a long time. 'Yours smell *different*,' he says quietly. He buys one cup, takes one slow sip, and stares at the ceiling with an unreadable face.
different:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林走进来，说我们的热饮闻起来和他那里的____。
different:0.hook: He came back the next four nights and never said another word.

author:0.en: A tired man sets three identical books on the counter and asks for a bag. I notice his name on each cover. He is the *author*, buying his own books from us because, he says, the shop near his flat sold out. He looks more surprised than proud about that.
author:0.cnHint: 一位男士来买书，我发现他正是这些书的____，他自己也觉得很意外。
author:0.hook: He left one copy behind, open to a page with a sentence underlined twice.
author:0.line: 'I am the *author* — but I still need to read it again to remember how it ends.'

increase:0.en: The Manager pins a new chart by the coffee machine showing a steady *increase* in late-night cup sales over three months. He looks proud. Tang points out that most of those cups are the ones we drink ourselves on slow nights. The Manager takes the chart down without a word.
increase:0.cnHint: 店长贴出一张图表，显示深夜咖啡销量的____，但阿糖说破了真相。
increase:0.hook: That same chart appeared again the next morning, with two columns quietly erased.
increase:0.line: 'Look — a clear *increase* in sales! This chart does not lie.'

university:0.en: Two students collapse into the corner seats at 4 a.m., textbooks stacked like small walls around them. One tells me their *university* exam starts in five hours. I quietly slide two extra napkins onto their table so they can keep writing notes. They do not look up, but one mouths thank you.
university:0.cnHint: 两位学生深夜备考，说他们的____考试还有五小时就开始了。
university:0.hook: One of their notebooks had tomorrow's date crossed out and rewritten three times.
university:0.line: 'Our *university* exam is at nine — we cannot afford to sleep yet.'

turn:0.en: At 5 a.m. the sky outside begins to *turn* a pale grey, and the store fills with the smell of the first fresh bread delivery. A small girl walks in holding her grandfather's hand, points at the bread, and says she has been waiting all night for this exact moment. Her grandfather buys her two loaves.
turn:0.cnHint: 天空开始____成淡灰色，一个小女孩和爷爷走进来，等的就是新鲜面包。
turn:0.hook: She pressed her face to the warm loaf and whispered something into it.
turn:0.line: 'Watch the sky *turn* — that is how we know the bread is almost here.'

actually:0.en: The store looked empty at midnight, but it was *actually* full of quiet activity. The Manager was counting receipts behind the counter, Tang was restocking the cold drinks shelf, and I stood near the door, pretending to look busy while learning everyone's routine.
actually:0.cnHint: 午夜的便利店____比看起来热闹得多。
actually:0.hook: Then a regular customer walked in, and everyone suddenly moved faster.
actually:0.line: It *actually* gets busier after midnight — just wait.

themselves:0.en: Two elderly women came in every night at eleven. They never asked for help. They moved through the snack aisle slowly, reading every label, talking softly to *themselves*, comparing prices with great seriousness, as if choosing the right biscuit was the most important decision of the evening.
themselves:0.cnHint: 两位老太太每晚都自己____逛零食货架。
themselves:0.hook: Tonight, one of them slipped a small note under a bag of crackers.
themselves:0.line: They always talk to *themselves* like that — it's their way.

person:0.en: Lin came to check on our store again, notebook in hand. She was the kind of *person* who noticed everything — the angle of the price tags, the gap on the bread shelf, the flicker of the light above the register. I watched her carefully from behind a display of cup noodles.
person:0.cnHint: 林是一个会注意到一切细节的____。
person:0.hook: She paused at the register and smiled at me a little too long.
person:0.line: I'm just the kind of *person* who pays close attention.

without:0.en: Tang could restock an entire shelf *without* making a single sound. I watched in quiet admiration as she moved cans and packets into perfect rows, never dropping anything, never bumping the shelves. The Manager noticed too, and gave a small approving nod from across the store.
without:0.cnHint: 唐能____发出任何声音地把货架整理得整整齐齐。
without:0.hook: But tonight, one tin rolled off and knocked something hidden behind the shelf.
without:0.line: I can do this whole shelf *without* waking anyone outside.

among:0.en: *Among* all the items on the late-night sale table, a small box of moon cakes sat alone, half-hidden under a bag of chips. It had been there for three days. The Manager kept moving it to a better spot each morning, but by midnight it was always pushed aside again.
among:0.cnHint: 在促销台上的所有商品____，那盒月饼总是被冷落。
among:0.hook: Tonight, someone finally picked it up — and then put it back.
among:0.line: That one is *among* the best we have, honestly.

suppose:0.en: A man in a raincoat stood at the hot food counter for a long time, staring at the steamed buns. 'I *suppose* I'll take two,' he finally said, more to himself than to me. He paid with exact change, as if he had been planning this purchase all day.
suppose:0.cnHint: 雨衣男子盯着包子看了很久，才____自己要买两个。
suppose:0.hook: He came back twenty minutes later and stared at the shelf again.
suppose:0.line: I *suppose* one more wouldn't hurt — wrap it up, please.

health:0.en: Tang kept a small handwritten chart behind the counter. It tracked which customers bought what — not for sales, she explained, but because she worried about people's *health*. The man who bought salty chips every night, the woman who only ever took energy drinks — she noticed them all.
health:0.cnHint: 唐用一张小表格默默关注着常客们的____状况。
health:0.hook: One name on the chart had a small red circle around it.
health:0.line: I just think *health* matters, even here at 2 a.m.

mean:0.en: The Manager pointed to a handwritten sign above the register. 'Smile.' I wasn't sure what he *meant* at first — was it a rule, a request, or just advice? By the third hour of the shift, when a tired student bought instant noodles without a word, I began to understand.
mean:0.cnHint: 店长指着那块'微笑'的牌子，我慢慢明白了它____什么。
mean:0.hook: The student came back later — just to say thank you.
mean:0.line: I *mean* it — a smile costs nothing, not even energy.

human:0.en: The store is quiet at 3 a.m. A regular customer shuffles in wearing slippers and reaches for a cup of hot soup. He wraps both hands around it and sighs. 'There is something very *human* about needing warm soup in the middle of the night,' Tang says from behind the counter, smiling.
human:0.cnHint: 深夜，一位常客来买热汤，阿糖感叹这是一种很____的需求。
human:0.hook: The old man paid, then left a folded note under the cup.
human:0.line: 'There is something very *human* about needing warm soup in the middle of the night.'

large:0.en: A delivery worker rushes in just before four and drops a *large* bag of coins on the counter — all small change from a long shift. He counts each coin slowly, buying two rice balls and a hot drink. The Manager watches without a word. He comes in every Thursday at this exact time.
large:0.cnHint: 一位配送员带着一大袋零钱来结账，买了两个饭团和一杯热饮。
large:0.hook: Last Thursday he did not come, and the Manager waited by the door.
large:0.line: 'Sorry, I only have a *large* bag of coins tonight — is that okay?'

end:0.en: The store is quiet at the *end* of each night. I sweep the floor slowly, listening to the hum of the drink fridges. Tang always leaves a small sticky note on the counter before going home. Tonight the note just says: 'Check the back shelf.' I wonder what he means.
end:0.cnHint: 每天深夜____，我总会发现同事唐留下的便条。
end:0.hook: The back shelf holds something I was never meant to find.
end:0.line: 'Every shift has an *end*, but this one feels different,' Tang said quietly.

important:0.en: The Manager calls me over before the morning rush. He holds a small notebook and looks serious. 'This is *important*,' he says, tapping the page. 'These are our regular customers. Learn their faces. Learn their orders.' I nod and take the notebook. The first name on the list is simply: Lin.
important:0.cnHint: 店长严肃地告诉我，有件事很____。
important:0.hook: Lin's name has a red circle around it, and no explanation.
important:0.line: 'Learning their names is *important*,' the Manager said, tapping the notebook.

cause:0.en: A small puddle near the door is the *cause* of three near-falls tonight. I mop it up each time, but it keeps coming back. Tang watches from behind the counter and shakes his head. 'That corner always leaks when it rains,' he says. Outside, the rain is getting heavier.
cause:0.cnHint: 角落里的水渍是今晚好几次险些滑倒的____。
cause:0.hook: Tang glances at the ceiling, and I follow his eyes upward.
cause:0.line: 'That puddle is the *cause* of all our trouble tonight,' Tang muttered.

accord:0.en: Lin walks in just before two in the morning and picks up the same warm drink without a word. We move in perfect *accord*: I scan the item, she taps her card, we exchange a small nod. No hello, no goodbye. Tang watches from the back room and raises one eyebrow at me.
accord:0.cnHint: 我和林之间的默契配合让我们之间产生了一种奇妙的____。
accord:0.hook: Tang mouths something I cannot quite read from across the store.
accord:0.line: 'We act in *accord* without ever saying a word,' I told Tang later.

result:0.en: I rearranged the snack wall by colour, just as an experiment. The *result* surprised me: customers stopped and stared, then bought two things instead of one. The Manager noticed the sales numbers and gave a slow nod of approval. Tang just stole a bag of chips and called it 'quality testing.'
result:0.cnHint: 我重新摆放零食架后，____让店长刮目相看。
result:0.hook: Tang's 'quality test' is now a nightly habit no one mentions.
result:0.line: 'The *result* of your idea was better than I expected,' the Manager admitted.

recent:0.en: A regular I have not seen before comes in, looking tired. He buys a hot coffee and sits near the window. Tang leans over and whispers, 'He used to come every night. Not *recent*ly, though.' The man stares at the dark street outside, both hands wrapped around the cup.
recent:0.cnHint: 唐悄悄告诉我，这位熟客____没怎么来过。
recent:0.hook: The man leaves a folded note under his empty cup.
recent:0.line: 'He hasn't been here *recently*, and I've been a little worried,' Tang said.

start:0.en: Every shift has the same *start*: count the cash drawer, check the fridges, wipe the counter. But tonight the drawer is twenty yuan short and the fridge door is already open. Tang shrugs. I shrug back. The Manager's car is parked outside, which it should not be at midnight.
start:0.cnHint: 每班的____都有固定流程，但今晚一切都不对劲。
start:0.hook: The Manager's coat is still on the hook, but he is nowhere inside.
start:0.line: 'A good *start* to the shift means a quiet night,' Tang always says.

however:0.en: The store is warm and bright at three in the morning. Outside, the street is empty. I expect a long, dull stretch of nothing. *However*, the door swings open and a breathless woman rushes in, pressing a small package across the counter and saying, 'Please keep this safe until morning.'
however:0.cnHint: 我以为深夜会很无聊，____发生了意外的事。
however:0.hook: The package is ticking, but probably not in a dangerous way.
however:0.line: 'I'm usually calm. *However*, tonight is a little different,' she admitted.

view:0.en: The Manager stood behind the counter and looked out at the empty street. 'I *view* this store as more than a shop,' he said quietly. 'It is a small world.' He straightened a row of canned goods, then turned to me with a smile that felt like a test.
view:0.cnHint: 店长把这家店____成一个小小的世界，他的话让新来的店员若有所思。
view:0.hook: But why did his smile disappear when the door opened?
view:0.line: 'I *view* this store as more than just a shop.'

social:0.en: Late on Tuesday, an old man came in and bought nothing. He just stood near the magazine rack, watching people pass outside. Tang told me later that he came every night. 'He has no *social* life left,' Tang said softly. 'This store is his only contact with the world.'
social:0.cnHint: 唐告诉新店员，那位老人几乎没有任何____活动，每晚只来这里待一会儿。
social:0.hook: Then the old man turned and looked straight at me.
social:0.line: 'He has no *social* life — this place is all he has.'

skill:0.en: A young woman asked me to wrap a gift box. My fingers fumbled with the ribbon. She watched patiently. 'It is a *skill*,' she said, and gently showed me how to make a neat bow. In thirty seconds, the box looked perfect. She left without telling me who it was for.
skill:0.cnHint: 一位年轻女士教新店员包装礼盒，说这是一门____。
skill:0.hook: The gift had no name tag on it at all.
skill:0.line: 'Wrapping a box neatly is a real *skill*, you know.'

job:0.en: Just after midnight, a tired man in paint-covered clothes bought two meat buns and a bottle of water. He counted coins slowly. 'Long night?' I asked. He nodded. 'Second *job*,' he said simply. He ate standing at the small counter by the window, staring at nothing.
job:0.cnHint: 一个疲惫的男人告诉新店员，这是他的第二份____。
job:0.hook: He left one coin on the counter and walked into the dark.
job:0.line: 'This is my second *job* — I finish at four every morning.'

business:0.en: Lin came in just before two in the morning, carrying a folder thick with papers. She bought black coffee and sat at the corner table. 'Still working?' I asked. She looked up with sharp eyes. '*Business* does not sleep,' she said. Then she opened her folder and ignored me completely.
business:0.cnHint: 林深夜带着文件来买咖啡，说____是不睡觉的。
business:0.hook: One page slid to the floor — it had our store's name on it.
business:0.line: '*Business* does not sleep, and neither do I.'

eat:0.en: A small boy came in holding his mother's hand. He pressed his nose to the glass of the hot-food case, fogging it up. 'Can I *eat* one of those?' he whispered. His mother checked her purse. I quietly added an extra bun to the bag. The boy's eyes went wide.
eat:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩想____热食柜里的食物，店员悄悄多加了一个包子。
eat:0.hook: His mother looked at the bag, then looked at me.
eat:0.line: 'Mum, can I *eat* one of those steamed buns, please?'

healthy:0.en: A woman in running clothes stopped in at half past one. She read every label before choosing a small pack of nuts. 'Is this *healthy*?' she asked, holding it up. I checked the back. Low salt, no added sugar. 'Looks good,' I said. She nodded firmly and bought four packs.
healthy:0.cnHint: 一位女士深夜跑步后进来，认真查看零食是否____。
healthy:0.hook: She comes in every night, but she never looks tired.
healthy:0.line: 'Tell me honestly — is this snack actually *healthy*?'

place:0.en: Around three in the morning, the store felt very still. I leaned on the counter and looked around: the warm light, the quiet hum of the fridge, the smell of coffee. This tiny *place* had its own slow heartbeat. Then the door chimed, and a woman in a nurse's uniform walked in.
place:0.cnHint: 深夜三点，新店员感受到这个小小的____有自己的生命。
place:0.hook: The nurse's hands were shaking as she reached for the shelf.
place:0.line: 'This little *place* feels warmer than anywhere else at night.'

likely:0.en: The store was quiet after midnight. I was tidying the snack shelf when the door opened. An old man in slippers shuffled in and headed straight for the warm drinks corner. The Manager leaned over and whispered, 'He's *likely* here for the canned soup. He comes every cold night.'
likely:0.cnHint: 店长悄悄告诉我，这位老人____每晚都来买一样的东西。
likely:0.hook: But tonight the old man picked up something else entirely.
likely:0.line: 'He is *likely* our most loyal regular, so treat him well.'

experience:0.en: Tang had worked the night shift for two years. When I knocked over a whole row of bottled tea on my first night, she just laughed softly and helped me clean up. 'Don't worry,' she said. 'With *experience*, you stop knocking things over. Mostly.' I wasn't sure whether 'mostly' was meant to comfort me.
experience:0.cnHint: 同事用自己的____安慰第一天手忙脚乱的我。
experience:0.hook: Then she pointed at a crack in the ceiling and went oddly quiet.
experience:0.line: 'Trust me, *experience* is the only teacher that actually works here.'

lot:0.en: A young woman dumped her bag on the counter and spread out a *lot* of small coins, counting slowly under the fluorescent light. She was buying a single rice ball and a carton of milk. The Manager pretended to check the stock room so she could count without feeling watched.
lot:0.cnHint: 一位女生用____零钱买了最简单的晚餐。
lot:0.hook: She left a tiny folded paper crane on the counter before walking out.
lot:0.line: 'I have a *lot* of small coins tonight — sorry about that.'

public:0.en: Someone had taped a hand-written notice on the *public* board near the entrance: 'Lost: one orange cat, answers to Dumpling.' Below it, three phone numbers were listed in different handwriting, as if strangers had added their own contacts one by one, all hoping to help.
public:0.cnHint: 店门口的____告示栏上贴着一张寻猫启事，陌生人们纷纷留下了联系方式。
public:0.hook: That night, a regular came in and stared at the notice for a very long time.
public:0.line: 'Can I put my notice on the *public* board by the door?'

example:0.en: Lin ran the small bookshop across the street and often came in for late-night coffee. She was always neat, always polite, always said thank you twice. Tang nudged me one evening and said, 'Watch her. She's a good *example* of how to treat people in a small neighbourhood.' I started paying closer attention after that.
example:0.cnHint: 同事让我把对街书店老板当作待人接物的____。
example:0.hook: The next night, Lin arrived looking nothing like her usual self.
example:0.line: 'She sets a good *example* — I try to copy her attitude every shift.'

whether:0.en: A teenager stood in front of the cold drinks section for almost five minutes, moving his lips silently. He picked up a green tea, put it back, picked up a fruit juice, put it back. Tang walked over and said, 'I can never decide *whether* to choose tea or juice either. I always end up with both.' He laughed and grabbed one of each.
whether:0.cnHint: 同事用一句话帮纠结的少年决定了____买茶还是买果汁。
whether:0.hook: He paid quickly and then asked Tang a completely unrelated question.
whether:0.line: 'I just can not decide *whether* the tea or the juice is better tonight.'

focus:0.en: The store had a small television mounted high on the wall, usually showing a quiet music channel. But tonight the *focus* of every customer's attention was a tiny spider making its way slowly across the screen. Nobody spoke. Four people stood with their necks tilted back, drinks in hand, completely still.
focus:0.cnHint: 一只小蜘蛛爬上了电视屏幕，成了全店顾客的____。
focus:0.hook: Then the spider disappeared behind the television and someone actually groaned.
focus:0.line: 'The *focus* of this whole store just shifted to a spider, I think.'

avoid:0.en: I learned quickly that the mop bucket near the back had a slow leak. Tang had drawn a small arrow on the floor in marker to warn people. 'Step around it,' she told me on day one. 'The Manager keeps forgetting to fix it.' I tried to *avoid* the wet patch all night, but at 3 a.m. I forgot.
avoid:0.cnHint: 同事提醒我要____地板上漏水的拖把桶，但我在凌晨三点还是踩到了。
avoid:0.hook: The sound I made woke up the cat sleeping on the top shelf.
avoid:0.line: 'Just *avoid* the wet spot near the back — trust me on that one.'

less:1.en: The rain had stopped, but the street outside was still wet. I stepped out to bring in the sign when I noticed an old man moving *less* than a metre from the door, counting coins under the lamp. He looked up, smiled, and said nothing. He came in every rainy night, the Manager had told me. Always bought one thing.
less:1.cnHint: 一位老人在门口昏黄的路灯下数硬币，他每个雨夜都会来买一样东西。
less:1.hook: But tonight he reached for something he had never bought before.
less:1.line: 'I need *less* change this time — I saved up.'

information:1.en: A courier on a bicycle stopped outside and taped a small note to our door. I read it: a list of street numbers with question marks. He knocked and asked if I had any *information* about a new block of flats nearby. I checked my phone, found the address, and wrote it down for him.
information:1.cnHint: 一位快递员骑车停在门口，想打听附近新公寓楼的____。
information:1.hook: The address I wrote down turned out to belong to someone we both knew.
information:1.line: 'Do you have any *information* about the new building on this street?'

paragraph:1.en: Just after two in the morning, a young woman sat on the step outside our door, notebook open, pen moving fast. I brought her a cup of warm water from inside. She looked up and said she was stuck on one *paragraph* of her essay and needed the cold air to think. She finished it ten minutes later and left without buying a thing.
paragraph:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一位女生坐在门口台阶上，为论文里卡住的____苦苦思索。
paragraph:1.hook: She left the notebook behind, and the last line was not about the essay at all.
paragraph:1.line: 'This one *paragraph* has beaten me for three nights straight.'

look:1.en: Tang was sweeping the path outside when a small dog sat down on the pavement and gave the store a long, steady *look*, ears up, tail still. Tang stopped sweeping. The dog did not move. We both waited. A minute later a man jogged around the corner calling a name, and the dog stood up and trotted off calmly.
look:1.cnHint: 一只小狗在店门口盯着橱窗久久打量，阿糖停下扫地，两人都等着它的下一步动作。
look:1.hook: The man who came to collect it glanced at our window in exactly the same way.
look:1.line: 'Give it a good *look* — it has been sitting there for five minutes.'

benefit:1.en: Lin appeared outside at half past midnight and stood under the awning, sheltering from a light drizzle. He pulled out a small leaflet and held it up to the light. It listed the *benefit* of a new store loyalty card. He studied it for a long time, then folded it and put it in his pocket without coming in.
benefit:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外避雨，借着灯光研究一张写满会员卡____的宣传单，却没有走进来。
benefit:1.hook: The leaflet was from our store, but no one here had printed it.
benefit:1.line: 'The main *benefit* is a free coffee every ten visits.'

contain:1.en: Just before dawn, a delivery van pulled up and the driver carried a small cardboard box to our door. The label said it could *contain* up to four kilograms of dried goods. He set it down, rang the bell, and drove away before I could ask who had sent it. I checked the Manager's number but the box had no name on it.
contain:1.cnHint: 天亮前，一个快递员送来一个无名纸箱，标签显示它能____四公斤货物，随后就开车走了。
contain:1.hook: Inside was something the Manager had never ordered but clearly needed.
contain:1.line: 'This box can *contain* everything you ordered — barely.'

direction:1.en: A teenager stopped in front of the store and spun slowly on the pavement, phone in one hand, a folded paper map in the other. He clearly needed *direction*, so I opened the door and pointed left toward the bus stop two corners away. He nodded, took three steps right, then turned left. We watched him until he disappeared.
direction:1.cnHint: 一个少年拿着手机和纸地图在门口原地转圈，显然需要有人给他指____。
direction:1.hook: He came back four minutes later from the opposite side of the street.
direction:1.line: 'Could you give me some *direction*? My phone just died.'

attach:1.en: Tang found a handwritten note on our door when he unlocked the gate at the start of the shift. Someone had used tape to *attach* it carefully at eye level, smoothing every corner. It read: 'Thank you for the umbrella on Tuesday. Left something in the green bag by the step.' The bag held six oranges and a small folded thank-you card.
attach:1.cnHint: 阿糖开门时发现有人用胶带把一张手写便条整齐地____在门上，袋子里装着橙子和感谢卡。
attach:1.hook: The handwriting matched the notes we had found on two earlier mornings.
attach:1.line: 'Someone came early to *attach* this — look how neat the tape is.'

end:1.en: At the far *end* of the street, a figure stood under the last lamp post, collar turned up against the cold. I could just make out the convenience store's glow from where I leaned on the doorframe, waiting for my first real night shift to begin. The figure did not move.
end:1.cnHint: 深夜，街道尽____处，一个身影一动不动地站在路灯下。
end:1.hook: The figure finally turned — and walked straight toward the store.
end:1.line: 'I always wait at the *end* of this street before I come in.'

important:1.en: Tang rushed out the side door, phone pressed to her ear, mouthing something urgent at me. She held up one finger — just one minute — and pointed at the register. I had no idea how to work it yet. Apparently, covering for a colleague on her *important* call was now part of the job.
important:1.cnHint: 同事接一个____的电话，把收银台丢给了新来的我。
important:1.hook: The phone call was not about work at all.
important:1.line: 'This is *important* — don't touch the register until I'm back.'

cause:1.en: A sudden gust swept a stack of flyers off the outdoor rack and sent them spinning down the pavement. I chased three of them into the road before I caught the last one. Nobody saw me, or so I thought. The wind was the *cause* of a small disaster — and a small audience.
cause:1.cnHint: 一阵风____了一场小小的混乱，我在街上狼狈地追传单。
cause:1.hook: Someone had been watching from across the street the whole time.
cause:1.line: 'What was the *cause* of all that noise outside just now?'

accord:1.en: Lin from the rival shop two doors down leaned against our outdoor rack, arms folded. We had never spoken, yet somehow — without a word — we both reached for the same fallen umbrella at the same moment. We looked at each other. 'Yours,' I said. We smiled. It was a small *accord*.
accord:1.cnHint: 我和竞争对手之间，悄悄达成了一个小小的____。
accord:1.hook: Lin slipped a folded note into my apron pocket before leaving.
accord:1.line: 'Maybe we can reach some kind of *accord* about the parking space out front.'

result:1.en: I swept the entrance for ten minutes, then stood back to check my work. A cat walked straight across the clean tiles, leaving tiny muddy prints in a neat line. The *result* was worse than before I started. I looked up to find the Manager watching from the doorway, one eyebrow raised.
result:1.cnHint: 我把门口扫得干干净净，但____却比扫之前还要糟糕。
result:1.hook: The Manager said nothing — just handed me a second broom.
result:1.line: 'What is the *result* when you leave the door open in the rain?'

recent:1.en: A regular customer paused outside, staring at the new sign I had taped to the window. He tilted his head, then knocked on the glass and pointed at it. I had written the weekly deals from memory, but I had copied last week's prices by mistake. My *recent* error was already drawing a crowd.
recent:1.cnHint: 我把____的价格牌写错了，门外已经有人围观。
recent:1.hook: One of those watching customers pulled out a camera.
recent:1.line: 'Have you seen the *recent* changes to the price list in the window?'

start:1.en: The Manager handed me a broom at five minutes to midnight and nodded toward the street. 'Sweep before the rush,' she said. There was no rush — it was a quiet Tuesday — but I swept anyway. That first long push of the broom across cold pavement felt like the real *start* of something.
start:1.cnHint: 午夜前，我拿着扫帚站在街上，感觉一切真正____了。
start:1.hook: A pair of boots stopped just beyond the circle of lamplight.
start:1.line: 'Every good shift has a *start* like this — just you and the empty street.'

however:1.en: The night air was cool and I was almost enjoying the quiet. *However*, the outdoor bin had tipped over, scattering wrappers across the pavement just as a pair of headlights swept around the corner. I grabbed a bag and started picking up rubbish fast. The car slowed. The window rolled down.
however:1.cnHint: 夜晚本来很平静，____垃圾桶倒了，还有辆车停在我旁边。
however:1.hook: A voice from the car said, 'Need a hand — or a witness?'
however:1.line: 'The street looks clean tonight; *however*, check behind the rack.'

derive:1.en: Just before two in the morning, an old man stopped under the street lamp outside and stared at our sign for a long time. When he finally came in, he told me he *derived* great comfort from knowing a light was always on out there. He bought one small bottle of warm tea and stood by the window for ten quiet minutes.
derive:1.cnHint: 一位老人说他从便利店的灯光中____到了安慰，然后在窗边静静地站了十分钟。
derive:1.hook: He left a folded note under the bottle he never opened.
derive:1.line: 'I *derive* more peace from that little lamp than from anything else on this street.'

report:1.en: Tang was halfway through a midnight snack when a schoolboy in a heavy coat rushed in, waving a piece of paper. It was his end-of-term *report*, and every subject had a red stamp meaning 'excellent.' He bought a small cake to celebrate alone on the steps outside, grinning at the cold sky.
report:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩冲进店里，挥舞着他拿到优秀成绩的____，买了块小蛋糕一个人庆祝。
report:1.hook: But the last page of the report was still folded tight and unopened.
report:1.line: 'My *report* says I passed everything — even the subject I thought I failed!'

research:1.en: A tired woman in a heavy coat came in around three and spread printed pages across the small corner table. She said she was doing *research* on why people buy snacks late at night. I slid a free coffee across the counter without a word. She looked up, then wrote something quickly in her notebook.
research:1.cnHint: 一位深夜来店的女士说她在做关于人们买零食习惯的____，我悄悄给她送了杯免费咖啡。
research:1.hook: She never told me what she wrote about me.
research:1.line: 'My *research* so far shows that kindness at three a.m. is very, very rare.'

different:1.en: Lin from the store across the street came in just before dawn with a serious look on his face. He walked every aisle twice, comparing our prices with a small notebook in hand. But he chose a drink we stock that his own shop does not. Every store is *different*, I suppose, even when they sell almost the same things.
different:1.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林来转了一圈，发现我们和他的店其实____，最后买了一瓶他自己店里没有的饮料。
different:1.hook: He paused at the door and almost said something, but didn't.
different:1.line: 'Your layout feels *different* from ours — somehow it makes me want to stay longer.'

author:1.en: A quiet young woman sat outside on the bench by our entrance for nearly an hour, typing on a small device. When she finally came in for hot water, I asked what she was working on. She smiled and said she was an *author* finishing the last chapter of her first book, right here, under our lamp.
author:1.cnHint: 一位年轻女性在店门口的长椅上坐了很久，她说自己是一位____，正在完成第一本书的最后一章。
author:1.hook: She asked me not to tell anyone the ending — not yet.
author:1.line: 'As an *author*, I find that the best last lines always come after midnight.'

increase:1.en: The Manager reviewed last month's numbers before leaving for the evening. He pointed to one small column and smiled. Night-shift sales showed a steady *increase* every week since I started. He patted the counter twice, said nothing else, and walked out into the cool early-morning air.
increase:1.cnHint: 店长指着上月的数据说，自从我开始上夜班，销售额一直在稳步____。
increase:1.hook: He left before I could ask if that meant a raise.
increase:1.line: 'The *increase* here is small, but it tells me something important about you.'

university:1.en: A young man with a rolled-up poster under his arm bought three energy drinks just after midnight. He said tomorrow was the first day of his *university* life and he had not slept at all. He spread the poster out on the counter to show me his new dorm room layout, drawn very carefully in pen.
university:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人说明天就是他____生活的第一天，他把精心绘制的宿舍平面图铺在柜台上给我看。
university:1.hook: One corner of the poster had a name crossed out and rewritten twice.
university:1.line: 'Starting *university* tomorrow — so tonight I am too excited to sleep at all.'

turn:1.en: Just after four, a woman jogging past our window suddenly stopped, looked left, looked right, then came in. She said she made a wrong *turn* somewhere and had been running in a circle for twenty minutes. She bought a small map of the neighbourhood from our rack, laughed at herself, and jogged back out.
turn:1.cnHint: 一位女跑步者进来说自己走错了____，在附近绕圈跑了二十分钟，买了一张地图才笑着离开。
turn:1.hook: The map she bought had a small handwritten mark near one corner of our street.
turn:1.line: 'I took a wrong *turn* by the old post box and ended up here — maybe that was lucky.'

actually:1.en: I stepped outside to tidy the small rack of umbrellas near the door. A woman stopped, stared at the price tag, and frowned. 'Too expensive,' she muttered. Then she checked her phone, looked at the dark clouds above, and *actually* put two umbrellas in her basket instead of one.
actually:1.cnHint: 一位女士原本嫌贵，但最后____买了两把伞。
actually:1.hook: She glanced back at me once, then hurried away into the dark.
actually:1.line: I *actually* need two — one always goes missing somehow.

themselves:1.en: A group of college students gathered on the pavement outside, debating loudly over a single receipt. None of them wanted to pay the full amount. I watched from the doorway as they argued *themselves* into a corner, until the quietest one simply put his card on the counter and ended it.
themselves:1.cnHint: 一群学生在门外为一张收据争来争去，最后____把自己逼进了僵局。
themselves:1.hook: The quiet one pocketed the receipt and smiled at no one in particular.
themselves:1.line: They talked *themselves* into a mess over three yuan.

person:1.en: On slow nights I like to guess things about the customers before they speak. A tall man in a raincoat came around the corner and paused under the awning. He was the kind of *person* who reads the label on everything before buying — I could tell by the way he tilted every bottle toward the light.
person:1.cnHint: 我试着在顾客开口前猜测他们的性格，一位雨衣男士让我觉得他是个____。
person:1.hook: He bought nothing, nodded once, and walked back into the rain.
person:1.line: Every *person* who reads labels this carefully has a story.

without:1.en: Just before dawn a delivery rider stopped his bike at the kerb and leaned in through the open door. He grabbed a warm meat bun from the basket by the till, dropped exact change on the counter, and left *without* a single word. The whole visit lasted maybe eight seconds.
without:1.cnHint: 一位外卖骑手拿了包子，留下零钱，____说一句话就走了。
without:1.hook: The same coins came back the very next morning, same amount.
without:1.line: He always leaves *without* even making eye contact.

among:1.en: After midnight a small crowd formed outside because a cat had climbed onto the canopy. Everyone looked up and offered advice. *Among* the onlookers was an elderly man I had never seen before. He said nothing, produced a tin of fish from his coat pocket, and the cat came straight down.
among:1.cnHint: 猫爬上了遮阳棚，围观的人们议论纷纷，____这些人中有一位老人悄悄解决了问题。
among:1.hook: The old man tucked the empty tin away and shuffled off without a word.
among:1.line: *Among* all those people, only he knew what to do.

suppose:1.en: Tang was restocking the drinks shelf outside when a boy on a skateboard nearly knocked the whole tray over. Tang caught it one-handed and barely flinched. 'I *suppose* you practise that,' the boy said, genuinely impressed. Tang just shrugged and carried the tray inside as if nothing had happened.
suppose:1.cnHint: 一个滑板少年差点撞倒货架，阿糖单手接住，少年____这需要练习。
suppose:1.hook: The boy came back an hour later — this time walking, very carefully.
suppose:1.line: I *suppose* you've dropped that tray at least once before.

health:1.en: An older woman does slow morning stretches on the pavement beside our store every single day. She told me once that good *health* does not come from any bottle on our shelves, but she still buys one small yoghurt every morning — 'just in case,' she always says with a wink.
health:1.cnHint: 一位老太太每天在门口做晨练，她说____不是从货架上买来的，但她还是每天买一瓶酸奶。
health:1.hook: This morning she bought two yoghurts and said nothing about it.
health:1.line: Real *health* starts outside, not in there.

mean:1.en: Lin was covering the outdoor display when a child pointed at the small toy capsule machine near the entrance and pulled his mother's sleeve. Lin knelt down and spun the handle slowly so the boy could watch. 'Does that *mean* I can have one?' the boy asked. Lin looked at me. I looked at the ceiling.
mean:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩盯着扭蛋机，隔壁咖啡店的林慢慢转动把手，男孩问这____他可以得到一个。
mean:1.hook: The mother was already reaching for her purse before anyone answered.
mean:1.line: Does that *mean* we're splitting the cost, Lin?

likely:1.en: The street outside the store is quiet at two in the morning. A cat sits on the bin near the lamp post. The Manager steps out to check the delivery. 'That driver is *likely* late again,' he says, squinting down the empty road. A distant engine hums.
likely:1.cnHint: 店长站在门外，觉得送货司机____又要迟到了。
likely:1.hook: Then the headlights appeared — from the wrong direction.
likely:1.line: 'That driver is *likely* late again — third time this week.'

experience:1.en: Tang sweeps the pavement just before dawn. A small boy stops and watches with wide eyes. 'Want to try?' Tang offers the broom. The boy pushes it once, then grins. Tang laughs softly. In my short *experience* on night shift, small moments like this one always feel the biggest.
experience:1.cnHint: 在夜班短暂的____里，我发现小小的街头瞬间最令人难忘。
experience:1.hook: The boy pocketed something before he ran off.
experience:1.line: 'In my *experience*, even a short sweep teaches you something.'

lot:1.en: Friday evening, the pavement in front of the store fills up fast. Schoolbags, bikes, loud laughter — a *lot* of students arrive all at once, flooding the entrance. The Manager signals me to open the second register. I move quickly, but one face in the crowd catches my eye.
lot:1.cnHint: 周五傍晚，门前一下子来了____学生，把入口堵得水泄不通。
lot:1.hook: One student never joined the others inside.
lot:1.line: 'There are a *lot* of them tonight — more than last Friday.'

public:1.en: The bus stop just outside is a small *public* stage every morning. Office workers, grandmothers with trolleys, a man in a bright yellow coat — all waiting, all watching each other quietly. I lean on the door frame and watch too, glad no one has asked me to board just yet.
public:1.cnHint: 门外的公交站是一个小小的____舞台，每天早晨上演各种故事。
public:1.hook: The man in yellow got off at the same stop every single day.
public:1.line: 'This bus stop is basically a *public* living room at rush hour.'

example:1.en: Lin from the rival shop across the road crosses over to buy a coffee. She looks around, then says to me, 'Your shelf layout is a good *example* of how to use space well.' I blink. Coming from Lin, that is basically a trophy. She leaves before I find words to reply.
example:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林过来买咖啡，说我们的货架陈列是个很好的____。
example:1.hook: She came back ten minutes later with a tape measure.
example:1.line: 'Your layout is a good *example* — I might borrow the idea.'

whether:1.en: Rain starts without warning. Two strangers dash under the store's small awning and stand shoulder to shoulder. They do not speak. I watch through the glass, wondering *whether* they will share an umbrella or stay awkward and silent until the clouds pass. The rain shows no sign of stopping.
whether:1.cnHint: 两个陌生人躲在店外的雨棚下，我好奇他们____会共用一把伞。
whether:1.hook: One of them slowly reached into a bag.
whether:1.line: 'I am not sure *whether* to offer my umbrella or just wait.'

focus:1.en: Tang is restocking the rack outside when a pigeon lands on a bag of chips. He freezes. The *focus* of every customer walking by shifts instantly from their phones to the bird and then to Tang's very still face. A child starts giggling. Tang does not breathe for a long moment.
focus:1.cnHint: 一只鸽子落在门外货架上，所有路人的____一下子转向了阿糖和那只鸟。
focus:1.hook: The pigeon then knocked over three more bags.
focus:1.line: 'Everyone's *focus* is on the pigeon — just shoo it, Tang!'

avoid:1.en: Lin crosses the street but takes a long curve around the postbox. I notice she does this every single night. The Manager leans over and whispers, 'She used to bump into that postbox badly — twice.' I make a quiet note to myself: *avoid* asking her about it. Ever.
avoid:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林每晚都绕路____那个邮筒，背后似乎有个尴尬的故事。
avoid:1.hook: Tonight she bumped into it anyway.
avoid:1.line: 'I always *avoid* that postbox — don't ask me why.'

view:1.en: Before my first shift, the Manager walked me to the corner outside the store and pointed down the quiet street. 'From here you can *view* everything — who is coming, who is leaving, who looks lost.' I nodded, trying to look like I already knew what I was doing.
view:1.cnHint: 店长带我到门口，说这里的____让我们能掌握街上的一切动静。
view:1.hook: Then he pointed at one shadow and said nothing.
view:1.line: 'From this spot you can *view* the whole street — remember that.'

social:1.en: A tall man in a neat coat stopped just outside the store every night, checking his phone with a small frown. He never came in. Tang whispered that the man had no *social* life at all — no calls, no messages, just weather updates. I was not sure Tang was right.
social:1.cnHint: 唐同事说那个常在门外站着的男人完全没有____生活。
social:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, the man looked up and smiled at someone.
social:1.line: 'He has zero *social* life — just him and his weather app.'

skill:1.en: An old woman set up a small folding table just outside our door each morning and repaired umbrellas with quiet, certain hands. Her *skill* drew a little crowd some days — people stood in a half-circle, watching in silence. I started leaving the door open so I could watch too.
skill:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在门外修伞，她的____吸引了不少人围观。
skill:1.hook: One morning her table was gone, and a single umbrella leaned against our wall.
skill:1.line: 'Watch her hands — that *skill* takes thirty years to earn.'

job:1.en: I overheard Lin on the phone outside the store, voice low and quick. 'I finished the *job*, okay? Every shelf, every label, every price.' He hung up, smoothed his jacket, and walked past me without a word. It was only later I realised he had been talking about his shift at a rival shop.
job:1.cnHint: 林在店门外打电话，悄悄汇报自己完成了某个____。
job:1.hook: He had a second notebook tucked inside his jacket.
job:1.line: 'I finished the *job* — every single shelf is done.'

business:1.en: A woman in a yellow scarf stood outside every Thursday, handing out small cards. 'Flower delivery, fresh daily,' she said to anyone who passed. I asked the Manager about her. He smiled. 'She started her *business* right here on this corner, three years ago. We keep each other company.'
business:1.cnHint: 一位常客在门外宣传自己的____，已经坚持了三年。
business:1.hook: That Thursday she handed me a card and winked.
business:1.line: 'This corner is where I started my *business* — good luck to us both.'

eat:1.en: Just after two in the morning a boy in a school uniform sat on the kerb outside and opened a convenience-store rice box from somewhere else. He began to *eat* very slowly, staring at the empty road. I stepped out and offered him a hot drink. He looked up, surprised anyone had noticed.
eat:1.cnHint: 深夜一个男孩坐在路边独自____，我走出去递给他一杯热饮。
eat:1.hook: He said he came here every night, but this was the first time anyone spoke.
eat:1.line: 'You should *eat* something warm — it is nearly three in the morning.'

healthy:1.en: Lin jogged past the store before every shift, waving as he went. One evening he stopped, slightly out of breath, and told me that staying *healthy* was the only way to survive night work. Then he bought two cream buns and ate them both before the door closed behind him.
healthy:1.cnHint: 林每次上班前都跑步，声称保持____是熬夜班的唯一方法。
healthy:1.hook: He was back in five minutes for a third bun.
healthy:1.line: 'Staying *healthy* is the only way to survive this job, trust me.'

place:1.en: The Manager showed me a chalk mark on the pavement just outside the entrance. 'Stand on this *place* when it is slow,' he said. 'You can see the whole street and the whole shop at once.' It was a small scuffed X, worn almost flat. Someone had been standing there for years.
place:1.cnHint: 店长指着门口地上一个粉笔记号，说这个____是观察一切的最佳位置。
place:1.hook: I looked down and saw the chalk was not chalk at all.
place:1.line: 'Stand on this *place* — you will see everything you need to see.'

human:1.en: I was sweeping the pavement outside the store just after midnight when I noticed something odd. A small brown dog sat perfectly still beside the lamp-post, watching every *human* who walked past, as if taking careful notes. It had been there for an hour. Then Tang came out and froze.
human:1.cnHint: 深夜，一只小狗坐在路灯旁，盯着每一个路过的____，唐走出店门后愣住了。
human:1.hook: The dog looked at Tang like it already knew him.
human:1.line: 'Every *human* it watches ends up coming into our store,' Tang whispered.

large:1.en: A delivery van pulled up at the corner just before dawn and the driver began stacking boxes on the pavement. The pile grew and grew until it formed a *large* wall of cardboard outside our door, blocking half the street. I stepped outside to count the boxes. Lin was already there, smiling.
large:1.cnHint: 黎明前，一辆送货车停在路口，搬下了____一堆纸箱，把半条街都堵住了，林已经站在那里笑着了。
large:1.hook: Lin's smile was the kind that hides a plan.
large:1.line: 'A *large* order like this means the Manager expects a very busy day,' Lin said.

less:2.en: A folded note sat under the door when I arrived for my shift. I opened it and found *less* writing than I expected — just four words: 'Watch the back shelf.' I stared at it for a moment, then tucked it into my apron pocket and walked slowly to the back of the store.
less:2.cnHint: 我上班时发现门缝里有张纸条，上面的字比想象中____得多。
less:2.hook: The back shelf held nothing unusual — yet.
less:2.line: 'There is *less* here than I thought, but enough to worry me.'

information:2.en: A regular customer, an older man with a canvas bag, pushed a folded flyer across the counter without a word. The flyer was packed with tiny print — delivery times, prices, a map. 'Too much *information*,' I said, laughing softly. He did not laugh. He tapped one line with his finger and left.
information:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客递来一张传单，上面的____多得让人眼花缭乱。
information:2.hook: The line he tapped had our store's address circled in red.
information:2.line: 'Too much *information* on one small page is never an accident.'

paragraph:2.en: A handwritten letter had been slipped into the magazine rack near the window. Most of it was in neat, careful English. The final *paragraph* was different — the handwriting shook, the words were crossed out twice, and at the end someone had written simply: 'Please keep this safe.' I did not know who had left it.
paragraph:2.cnHint: 杂志架里藏着一封信，最后一____的字迹明显和前面不同。
paragraph:2.hook: The name at the bottom belonged to someone I had already met.
paragraph:2.line: 'Read the last *paragraph* again — slowly this time.'

look:2.en: Tang came in early, still wearing her coat, and went straight to the lost-and-found box behind the counter. She gave the box a long, careful *look*, then lifted out a small red notebook. She held it up to the light, said nothing, and placed it quietly in her bag before clocking in as if nothing had happened.
look:2.cnHint: 同事阿糖来得很早，对失物箱投去了意味深长的一____。
look:2.hook: That red notebook had been in the box for exactly three days.
look:2.line: 'Give it one more *look* before you decide it means nothing.'

benefit:2.en: The Manager left a printed memo on the staff board. It listed a new rule: clerks could take one unsold sandwich at the end of each shift. 'The *benefit* is simple,' he had written at the bottom. 'Happy staff, less waste.' I read it twice, smiled, and made a mental note to stay until closing.
benefit:2.cnHint: 店长贴出一张通知，说明新规定对员工的____。
benefit:2.hook: Lin had already crossed out her name and written mine in the sign-up column.
benefit:2.line: 'The *benefit* here is real — do not let Lin take it first.'

contain:2.en: I found a small box tucked behind the water bottles on the lowest shelf. It was sealed with tape and had no label. I shook it gently — something shifted inside. A note stuck to the bottom read: 'Does *contain* fragile items. Do not open.' I set it on the counter and waited for someone to claim it.
contain:2.cnHint: 货架最低层藏着一个小箱子，便条上写着它____易碎物品。
contain:2.hook: No one came to claim it by morning.
contain:2.line: 'This box does *contain* something important, I promise you that.'

direction:2.en: Lin walked in during my third night shift and stood in the middle of the aisle, turning slowly. I asked if she needed help. She said she was looking for the new display of imported snacks. 'The Manager gave me no *direction* at all,' she said, sounding annoyed. I pointed left. She walked right, just to be different.
direction:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林进店后找不到新货架，抱怨店长没给任何____。
direction:2.hook: She found something near that right shelf that stopped her cold.
direction:2.line: 'He gave me zero *direction*, so now I decide for myself.'

attach:2.en: A small envelope was clipped to the staff notice board with a single paper clip. Someone had used tape to *attach* a tiny dried flower to the front of it. The envelope was addressed to 'the night clerk' in looping handwriting. Inside was a receipt — and on the back, a question I did not know how to answer.
attach:2.cnHint: 有人把一朵小干花____在留给夜班店员的信封上。
attach:2.hook: The question on the receipt was about something only I knew.
attach:2.line: 'Why did you *attach* this flower — what are you trying to tell me?'

derive:2.en: A folded note fell out of a returned umbrella. I opened it and read: 'I *derive* great comfort from knowing this store is always lit.' No name, no date. Just neat handwriting on a torn page. I pinned it above the register and wondered who had left it.
derive:2.cnHint: 一张纸条从还回来的雨伞里掉了出来，店员把它贴在了收银台上方。
derive:2.hook: That same handwriting appeared again the very next night.
derive:2.line: 'I *derive* great comfort from knowing this store never closes.'

report:2.en: Lin came in at midnight carrying a thick *report* under her arm. She set it on the counter, bought two cans of coffee, and stared at the cover without opening it. 'Heavy reading?' I asked. She laughed quietly. 'Heavy enough to keep me here until morning,' she said, and claimed a corner table.
report:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜带着一份厚厚的____来到店里，在角落坐了下来。
report:2.hook: By four in the morning, the report was still unopened.
report:2.line: 'This *report* won't read itself, so I need very strong coffee.'

research:2.en: A man in a worn jacket asked if he could sit and use the outlet near the window. He spread out notebooks covered in tiny writing. 'What are you working on?' I asked. 'Street-food *research*,' he said, holding up a page full of soup names and prices. I offered him a free sample of our instant noodles.
research:2.cnHint: 一位男士在靠窗的位置展开笔记本，专心做关于街头食物的____。
research:2.hook: One soup name on his list matched our newest shelf item exactly.
research:2.line: 'My *research* shows this block has the best late-night snacks.'

different:2.en: Tang restocked the drinks fridge and stepped back. 'Something feels *different* tonight,' she said, tilting her head. We both looked around. Then I noticed it: someone had turned every price tag upside down on the top shelf. Tang laughed. I did not laugh. I had just finished setting those tags an hour ago.
different:2.cnHint: 阿糖觉得今晚店里有什么地方____，两人一起找原因。
different:2.hook: The security camera showed no one going near that shelf.
different:2.line: 'Something feels *different* in here — did you move the shelf?'

author:2.en: A quiet woman asked for a pen. She sat at the small corner table, opened a notebook, and wrote without stopping for twenty minutes. When she left she forgot a bookmark. On it, in small print, was her name and the words 'debut *author*, signing copies this Saturday.' I put the bookmark by the register.
author:2.cnHint: 一位女士在角落写了二十分钟，离开时落下了一张印有"____"字样的书签。
author:2.hook: The book title on the bookmark matched our one shelf of novels.
author:2.line: 'As a new *author*, I do my best writing after midnight, oddly.'

increase:2.en: The Manager taped a small sign near the door: 'Hot drink prices will *increase* by one yuan next Monday.' By midnight, six regulars had come in early just to stock up on coffee vouchers. Tang counted the voucher pile and raised an eyebrow at me. Neither of us had expected that kind of loyalty to a hot drink.
increase:2.cnHint: 店长贴出涨价通知后，当晚顾客的购买量出现了明显的____。
increase:2.hook: One customer bought enough vouchers to last an entire year.
increase:2.line: 'A small *increase* in price means I buy all my vouchers right now.'

university:2.en: A young man emptied his pockets onto the counter: coins, a bus pass, and a crumpled letter. 'Good news?' I asked. He smoothed the letter flat. It was a *university* acceptance notice, still unopened until that very moment. He read it under the bright store light and let out one long breath. Then he bought the most expensive cake we had.
university:2.cnHint: 一位年轻人在店里当场拆开了一封____录取通知书。
university:2.hook: He asked me to keep the envelope as proof it was real.
university:2.line: 'I got into *university* — please tell me you sell celebration cake.'

turn:2.en: Just before three in the morning the old radio on the back shelf started to *turn* out a soft melody on its own. I had not touched it. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. The Manager, half asleep on his stool, opened one eye and said, 'It always does that. Just leave it.' He closed his eye again.
turn:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，收音机自己____开始播放音乐，让店员们吃了一惊。
turn:2.hook: The song it played was one none of us had ever heard before.
turn:2.line: 'Don't *turn* it off — that song means a good night for sales.'

actually:2.en: A folded note fell out of a returned umbrella left by the counter. I opened it, expecting a phone number or a shopping list. It *actually* contained a hand-drawn map of every late-night food stall within walking distance, with tiny stars marking the best ones. Someone had spent real time on this.
actually:2.cnHint: 收银台旁的雨伞里掉出一张纸条，上面____是一张手绘的深夜小吃地图。
actually:2.hook: The last star on the map pointed straight back to our store.
actually:2.line: 'It *actually* took me three weeks to draw that map.'

themselves:2.en: Two students came in just before two in the morning, arms full of notes. They picked out snacks without a word, then settled on the floor by the magazine rack and quizzed *themselves* in low, serious voices. I turned the overhead light up a little without asking.
themselves:2.cnHint: 两位学生在深夜悄悄进来，靠着杂志架____复习功课。
themselves:2.hook: One of them whispered a wrong answer, and the other just smiled.
themselves:2.line: 'We always quiz *themselves* — I mean, each other — here at night.'

person:2.en: Every regular pays a different way — card, coins, a crumpled note fished from a jacket pocket. But one *person* always leaves exact change on the counter before I even read the total, then walks out with a small wave. I have never once caught their face clearly.
person:2.cnHint: 有一位____总是在我报价前就把零钱放好，然后悄悄离开。
person:2.hook: Tonight the coins spelled out a different amount — three times too much.
person:2.line: 'I am the kind of *person* who always prepares in advance.'

without:2.en: Tang showed me the shelf-check routine on my first night. She moved through every aisle *without* looking at her notes, reading expiry dates the way other people read familiar street signs. I followed behind, scribbling everything down, feeling very new indeed.
without:2.cnHint: 阿糖教我盘点货架时，____看任何笔记就把所有日期背出来了。
without:2.hook: She paused at one shelf and said nothing for a long, odd moment.
without:2.line: 'I can do the whole store *without* stopping once — try me.'

among:2.en: The lost-and-found box under the counter holds a surprising collection: three umbrellas, a single glove, two phone chargers, and, *among* all of it, a small notebook filled with pressed flowers. I put it on top so the owner would spot it easily.
among:2.cnHint: 失物招领箱里____那些杂物中，藏着一本夹满压花的小本子。
among:2.hook: The notebook had no name, but the last page had our store's address.
among:2.line: 'My notebook was *among* all that stuff? I left it here on purpose.'

suppose:2.en: A man came in at four and stood in front of the warm drinks for a full two minutes. 'I *suppose* the jasmine tea,' he finally said, to himself more than to me. He paid, sat on the step outside, and stared at the empty street like he was waiting for an answer.
suppose:2.cnHint: 一位男士在热饮货架前站了很久，____还是拿了茉莉茶，然后坐在门外发呆。
suppose:2.hook: He came back five minutes later and bought a second one for someone.
suppose:2.line: 'I *suppose* that is the right choice — it usually is.'

health:2.en: The Manager taped a handwritten chart above the staff fridge listing which instant meals were lower in salt. 'Night shifts are hard on your *health*,' she said, not looking up from her clipboard. It was the most she had spoken to me all week, and it felt like being looked after.
health:2.cnHint: 店长在员工冰箱上贴了一张图，提醒大家注意____，这让我感觉被关心了。
health:2.hook: The chart had a small note at the bottom in a different handwriting.
health:2.line: 'Your *health* matters more than finishing every shelf tonight.'

mean:2.en: Lin from the store across the road slipped in at three to buy ice. We nodded — that is the usual greeting. 'Just because we compete does not *mean* we can not share a freezer emergency,' she said, then smiled before I could decide whether it was a joke.
mean:2.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林来借冰，说竞争并不____两家不能互相帮忙，笑着走了。
mean:2.hook: She left a small bag of her store's best biscuits on the counter.
mean:2.line: 'Compete does not *mean* we have to be unfriendly, you know.'

end:2.en: A folded note sat at the *end* of the lost-and-found shelf, behind an old umbrella nobody had claimed in weeks. I opened it and read three words in careful handwriting: 'Still waiting here.' I looked around the empty store. No one was inside. No one had been in for an hour.
end:2.cnHint: 我在失物招领架的____发现了一张字条，上面只有三个字。
end:2.hook: The handwriting matched the umbrella's gift tag exactly.
end:2.line: 'Check the *end* of the shelf — something there is not ours.'

important:2.en: Tang slid a sticky note across the counter without a word. It said: 'The lady who buys warm soy milk at 3 a.m. — her order is *important*, never get it wrong.' I nodded, puzzled. Tang had already turned back to stacking cups. The note had yesterday's date on it, and something like worry in the handwriting.
important:2.cnHint: 阿糖递给我一张便利贴，提醒我某位顾客的订单____不能搞错。
important:2.hook: I wondered what happened the last time someone got it wrong.
important:2.line: 'Her order is *important* — please, just remember that.'

cause:2.en: A small puddle near the drinks fridge had no clear *cause* — the floor was dry everywhere else, and no bottle was leaking. I put out a wet-floor sign just in case. Around two in the morning, a quiet regular in a yellow raincoat walked in, dripping steadily, and headed straight for that exact spot as if she already knew it was hers.
cause:2.cnHint: 饮料柜旁出现了一个来____不明的小水坑。
cause:2.hook: She smiled at the sign like she had seen it before.
cause:2.line: 'I wonder what could *cause* a puddle with no broken bottle near.'

accord:2.en: Lin walked in from the rival store across the street and placed a carton of eggs on our counter without a word. The Manager gave a small nod. By some silent *accord* the two of them had clearly reached long before I arrived, rival stores apparently helped each other with stock after midnight. I had so many questions.
accord:2.cnHint: 店长和隔壁咖啡店的林之间似乎有一种不言而喻的____，让我完全摸不着头脑。
accord:2.hook: The Manager just smiled and said, 'Old story — ask me in a year.'
accord:2.line: 'We reached an *accord* years ago — we help each other after midnight.'

result:2.en: I reorganised the snack shelf by colour, just to pass the slow hours. The *result* was a neat rainbow from yellow chips to dark chocolate at the far right. The Manager stopped, stared for a long moment, then took a single photo with their phone. They said nothing. They sent the photo somewhere. A reply came back in seconds — three identical wide-eyed faces.
result:2.cnHint: 我把零食架按颜色重新整理了一遍，____让店长拍照发给了某人。
result:2.hook: I still do not know who those three wide-eyed faces belong to.
result:2.line: 'Look at this *result* — someone here has too much free time and good taste.'

recent:2.en: Tucked behind the register was a small notebook filled with *recent* entries — dates, weather, and one odd detail per night: 'moth on the window,' 'man counted coins twice,' 'radio played the same song three times.' Tang caught me reading it and said, 'Every clerk keeps one.' They handed me a fresh, blank notebook. It was already warm, as if someone had been holding it.
recent:2.cnHint: 收银台后藏着一本记录____夜晚奇事的小册子。
recent:2.hook: The last entry was from last night, but I was the only clerk here.
recent:2.line: 'The *recent* entries are the ones worth reading most carefully, trust me.'

start:2.en: My first real night alone behind the counter was a quiet *start* — one customer in two hours, a man who bought a single battery and asked me to test it before he left. I tested it. It worked. He nodded as if this confirmed something important about me personally, then walked out into the dark without another word.
start:2.cnHint: 我独自值班的____出奇地平静，只有一位奇怪的顾客。
start:2.hook: He came back the next night with two batteries and the same careful look.
start:2.line: 'Every good clerk needs a quiet *start* — consider yourself lucky tonight.'

however:2.en: The Manager left a list of simple overnight tasks — tidy, restock, mop. Easy enough. *However*, task four read: 'If the radio turns itself on after 3 a.m., just let it play.' I checked the radio. It was not even plugged in. I wrote a question mark next to task four. By 3:10, I heard music.
however:2.cnHint: 店长留下的任务清单看似简单，____第四条让我背脊发凉。
however:2.hook: The song it played had no words, but somehow I knew all of it.
however:2.line: 'The nights here are calm, *however*, some things you simply do not question.'

human:2.en: A lost cat wandered in just after midnight and sat beside the snack shelf like it owned the place. I looked at it; it looked at me. Tang leaned over the counter and whispered, 'Every *human* who comes in tonight will probably try to adopt it.' Sure enough, the next customer walked straight past the drinks and crouched down on the floor.
human:2.cnHint: 一只迷路的猫溜进店里，阿糖说每个____进来的人都会想收养它。
human:2.hook: The cat ignored everyone — except the quiet woman who came in at 2 a.m.
human:2.line: 'Every *human* in this store after midnight has the same soft look in their eyes.'

large:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the back-room door before he went home: 'New stock in the *large* box by the fridge — please sort before 4 a.m.' I opened it and found, stacked in careful rows, about forty identical cans of red-bean soup. I counted twice. The note gave no further explanation.
large:2.cnHint: 店长留下纸条，让我整理冰箱旁那个____箱子里的新货。
large:2.hook: At 3 a.m., a regular came in and bought every single can without a word.
large:2.line: 'That *large* box has been here every Thursday night for two years, and I always buy it all.'

likely:2.en: A folded note was taped to the front door when I arrived for my shift. It said: 'If you find my blue umbrella, please keep it safe.' No name, no number. Tang said the umbrella was *likely* left by the quiet man who always buys warm milk at midnight — he had been in just an hour before.
likely:2.cnHint: 一张没有署名的纸条贴在门上，阿糖说那把伞____是某位常客落下的。
likely:2.hook: But the umbrella on our shelf had someone else's name written inside.
likely:2.line: 'That note is *likely* from the man who comes in every single night.'

experience:2.en: The Manager pulled me aside near the storage room and handed me a worn notebook. 'Every strange thing that happens on this shift is written here,' she said quietly. Reading it was quite an *experience* — one page described a customer who paid only in coins and always counted them out loud, twice.
experience:2.cnHint: 店长把一本记满夜班奇事的笔记本交给了我，阅读它是一次奇妙的____。
experience:2.hook: The last entry, dated just yesterday, had no ending — it stopped mid-sentence.
experience:2.line: 'Reading this notebook is quite an *experience*, I promise you that.'

lot:2.en: Tang was restacking the shelf near the window when a small box fell and burst open. Out spilled a *lot* of tiny paper stars — at least two hundred of them, each folded from strips of old receipt paper. A handwritten card underneath read: 'For whoever needs them most tonight.'
lot:2.cnHint: 一个盒子掉落后，里面滚出了____折纸星星，还附着一张小卡片。
lot:2.hook: The card had a name on the back, but the ink had smudged into one unreadable word.
lot:2.line: 'There is a *lot* of care folded into every one of these stars.'

public:2.en: Someone had left a small chalkboard leaning against the magazine rack. On it, in neat letters: 'Tonight's *public* announcement — the cat that visits this corner every Friday is named Biscuit. Please greet her properly.' I looked at Tang. Tang looked at me. Neither of us had put it there.
public:2.cnHint: 一块小黑板突然出现在杂志架旁，上面写着一则面向____的"公告"。
public:2.hook: By morning, three more messages had appeared on the board, all in different handwriting.
public:2.line: 'This *public* notice about the cat is the best thing I have read all week.'

example:2.en: The Manager kept a corkboard behind the counter covered in notes. 'This one,' she said, pointing to a receipt with a smiley face drawn on it, 'is my favourite *example* of why this job matters.' A customer had written on the back: 'You remembered my order. That made my whole day better.'
example:2.cnHint: 店长指着留言板上的一张收据，说它是这份工作意义的最好____。
example:2.hook: She never mentioned who that customer was, but her voice softened a little every time.
example:2.line: 'This receipt is the best *example* of why small things really matter.'

whether:2.en: A regular left a sealed envelope on the counter with just two words written on it: 'Open carefully.' Inside was a question on a folded slip of paper — '*Whether* the night shift ever feels lonely?' — and below it, a small hand-drawn map to the best spot on the roof to watch the city lights.
whether:2.cnHint: 一个常客留下了一封信，里面是一个关于____夜班会感到孤独的问题，还附了一张小地图。
whether:2.hook: The map was marked with a time: 3:47 a.m., circled twice.
whether:2.line: 'I always wonder *whether* the people working nights feel seen at all.'

focus:2.en: I found a pair of glasses resting on the drinks cooler, no case, no note. Tang said the woman who left them always comes in to read the small shelf of second-hand magazines. 'Her *focus* when she reads,' Tang said, 'is something else — the whole store could run out of stock and she would not notice.'
focus:2.cnHint: 一副眼镜被遗忘在饮料柜上，阿糖说那位常客读杂志时____极其专注。
focus:2.hook: She had underlined the same sentence in three different magazines, all from different years.
focus:2.line: 'Her *focus* when she reads makes the rest of the world go completely quiet.'

avoid:2.en: Tang pointed out a gap on the snack shelf where one row was always left empty. 'The Manager does that on purpose,' Tang whispered. 'She used to stock that row with something a regular loved, but that customer had to *avoid* it for health reasons now — so she keeps the space, just to remember them.'
avoid:2.cnHint: 货架上有一排故意空着，因为一位常客如今需要____某种食品，店长用空位来纪念他们。
avoid:2.hook: The regular had not been seen in over two months, and nobody said why.
avoid:2.line: 'I have to *avoid* that whole shelf now, but I still walk past it every time.'

view:2.en: A folded note sat under the door when I arrived. It was from the Manager: 'The shelf by the window is yours to arrange.' I climbed on a step-stool and looked out. The whole quiet street stretched below me, every lamp still glowing. From up here, the *view* was soft and wide, like the city was sleeping and trusted us to watch over it.
view:2.cnHint: 店员在整理窗边货架时，从高处____了整条安静的街道。
view:2.hook: But whose handwriting was on the second note, still tucked behind the shelf?
view:2.line: 'From up here the *view* makes every late shift feel worth it.'

social:2.en: Tang slid a flyer across the counter without a word. 'Community Board Night,' it read. I asked if we were supposed to go. Tang shrugged. 'The Manager says a store is a *social* place — people share more than money here.' I looked around at the small tables, the sticky notes customers left for each other. Maybe Tang was right.
social:2.cnHint: 阿糖给店员看了一张活动传单，说这家店本质上是一个____场所。
social:2.hook: One sticky note on the board simply read: 'I'll be back when I'm brave enough.'
social:2.line: 'A store is a *social* place — people share more than money here.'

skill:2.en: An older woman came in every Tuesday to buy a single envelope. Tonight she asked me to weigh it for her. My hands shook a little with the small postal scale. She watched, then gently moved my fingers to the right spot. 'That's the *skill*,' she said, calm as a teacher. She had clearly done this ten thousand times before.
skill:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客在买信封时，向店员展示了称重的____。
skill:2.hook: She never told me who she was writing to, but her letters always smelled faintly of dried flowers.
skill:2.line: 'Right there — that's the *skill*. Feel the balance before you read the number.'

job:2.en: I found a laminated card taped inside the register drawer. It listed every task for the night shift in neat small print. At the bottom the Manager had added by hand: 'Your real *job* is to make whoever walks in at 3 a.m. feel less alone.' I read it twice. Then I tucked it back and waited for the door to open.
job:2.cnHint: 店长在收银机里留下了一张卡片，重新定义了夜班店员真正的____。
job:2.hook: Exactly at 3 a.m., someone pushed the door open — then stopped, as if surprised to find the lights on.
job:2.line: 'Your real *job* is to make whoever walks in at 3 a.m. feel less alone.'

business:2.en: Lin arrived just before midnight carrying a thick folder. 'Market study,' Lin said, dropping it on the counter with a thud. 'Your store does surprisingly good *business* for a corner spot.' I peeked at the charts inside — our store was circled in red. Lin snapped the folder shut before I could read further.
business:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着市场调研报告来访，对这家街角小店的____表示出乎意料的兴趣。
business:2.hook: Why was our little store circled in red on every single page?
business:2.line: 'You do surprisingly good *business* for a place most people walk past without looking.'

eat:2.en: Around 2 a.m. a teenage boy sat on the step outside with a small container of instant noodles, no hot water. He looked at it sadly. I waved him in, filled a cup at our hot-water station, and watched him *eat* slowly, both hands wrapped around the warm container. He didn't say thank you — he just nodded, which felt like more.
eat:2.cnHint: 一个深夜的少年在门外____着干泡面，店员悄悄帮他解决了热水问题。
eat:2.hook: He left a folded paper star on the counter and never came back — or so I thought.
eat:2.line: 'Come in and *eat* properly — the hot water is free and the step is cold.'

healthy:2.en: Tang kept a small notebook behind the register full of food facts. 'Is this *healthy*?' a child asked, holding up a bag of puffed rice snacks. Tang flipped to a page without looking. 'Eat one small bag, drink water, run around outside tomorrow — then yes,' Tang said. The child thought hard, then put a second bag back on the shelf.
healthy:2.cnHint: 一个小朋友拿着零食问阿糖这东西____不____，阿糖给出了出人意料的条件式回答。
healthy:2.hook: The child's question was still written in Tang's notebook, with a small star drawn beside it.
healthy:2.line: 'One bag, some water, and fresh air tomorrow — then it is *healthy* enough.'

place:2.en: I was restocking the back shelf when I noticed something odd — a small ceramic cat sat between the soy sauce and the vinegar, smiling at the wall. No price tag. No explanation. Tang said only, 'It has always been there.' The Manager just smiled. Some things in this store had found their *place* long before any of us arrived.
place:2.cnHint: 店员在货架上发现了一只来历不明的陶瓷猫，它似乎早已找到了自己的____。
place:2.hook: That night someone came in, looked straight at the ceramic cat, and quietly said, 'Still here. Good.'
place:2.line: 'Everything in this store has found its *place* — even the things nobody put there on purpose.'
